Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

risk noun and verb

also danger, dangerous, risky, at your own risk, take a risk, run a risk, at risk, in danger

classical

Plaut. Bacch. 752: meō perīclō rem gerō
Cic. Rosc. Am. 110: perīculum adīre capitis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 107, 371

perīculum (perīclum), perīculī n.

noun, second declension

risk, danger

At your own risk: tuō perīculō (Traupman 107, 371). To run a risk: perīculum adīre or subīre; Traupman’s perīculum facere is in Plautus (Lewis & Short), though more often it means “make trial of”. In danger: in perīculō esse. Risky: perīculōsus (Cato Agr. praef. 1), anceps (Traupman 372).

Other words

  • discrīmen, discrīminis n. — a critical risk, a decisive moment

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 12: in perīculum ac discrīmen vocātur (Lewis & Short)

    To put at risk: in discrīmen vocāre.

  • ālea, āleae f. — a gamble, a risk (properly, dice)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Hor. C. 2.1.6: perīculōsae plēnum opus āleae

  • perīclitor, perīclitārī, perīclitātus sum — risk, put at risk; put to the test

    also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.11: salūs summa perīclitanda reī pūblicae (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “to put in peril, endanger, risk (rare but class.)”; more often “try, test”.

Examples

  • mea fīdūciā opus condūxī et meō perīclō rem gerō

    I’ve taken on the job on my own credit, and I’m running it at my own riskPlaut. Bacch. 752

  • perīculōsae plēnum opus āleae tractās et incēdis per ignīs suppositōs cinerī dolōsō

    you are handling a work full of dangerous risk, and walking over fires hidden under treacherous ashHor. C. 2.1.6–8

  • Caret perīclō, quī etiam cum est tūtus cavet.

    He runs no risk who takes care even when he is safe.Publil. Sent. C 32

See also lack, chance, safe journey.
